clue.text: Stupid people lacking college educator for ABC etc

indicators.note: lacking says one piece goes missing from the stupid people

parts.note: donkeys are dolts, stupid people
a don is a college lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Dimwits taught without their tutor are left stuck on the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A, B and C are musical keys, as are the other letters up to G.

clue.text: The panel rudely ignored occupant of room?

indicators.note: done rudely means done roughly, so these letters are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: A discussion panel rudely snubs the person sitting in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial elephant in the room is the obvious problem everyone pretends not to see.

clue.text: A new job not quite providing security

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a job or task

explanation.surface: Taking a fresh job that does not quite give a secure income.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is a source of stability and safety, something that holds you firm.

clue.text: Passed round edible tubers wrong way up and caused alarm

indicators.note: round says the first word goes around the other piece

parts.note: passed away means died

indicators.note: in a down clue, wrong way up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: yams are edible tubers

explanation.surface: Someone passed a plate of upside-down potatoes and caused a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'wrong way up' means the tubers read upwards; 'Passed' looks like handing something over but means died.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to fill them with alarm or distress, so having dismayed is having caused alarm.

clue.text: Implement obtained from second squalid home

parts.note: a hovel is a squalid dwelling

explanation.surface: A tool fetched from a second rundown house.
explanation.definitionFit: A shovel is a digging tool, a common garden implement.

clue.text: Old comedian's dance, ending in glide

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A veteran comic's dance routine finishes with a glide.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Hope was a famous American comedian of the last century.

clue.text: Fen country wife has dental treatment?

indicators.note: giving the word a treatment works its letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: A country wife from the Fens goes to the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fen is marshy land, a type of wetland.

clue.text: Smelly lout overturned chest of drawers, US fashion

parts.note: high meat smells, so high means smelly

indicators.note: overturned says the lout is turned around, reading backwards

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout

explanation.surface: A smelly hooligan knocks over an American chest of drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: Highboy is the American name for a tall chest of drawers on legs.

clue.text: Opposed to work's quality rating

parts.note: VS is short for versus, opposed to
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone set against the quality grading of a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: VSOP, Very Special Old Pale, is a grade marking the quality of brandy or cognac.

clue.text: Rash move to open up someone local shot by an amateur?

indicators.note: to open up says one piece is split open with the other placed inside

parts.note: a homie is slang for someone from your home town

indicators.note: a rash move is reckless, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A hasty move to confide in a neighbour, made by a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like an adjective for the move but is the anagram signal; the definition plays on shot as filmed, not fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A home movie is a film made by an amateur, footage shot by family members.

clue.text: Ration one's expressions of appreciation when abroad? That's barbarous!

parts.note: merci is French for thank you
to ration your thanks is to say them less

explanation.surface: A tourist stingy with their thank-yous is called a savage.
explanation.walkthrough: Rationing one's foreign thanks means saying MERCI LESS often.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarous behaviour is cruel and pitiless, showing no mercy at all.

clue.text: Rocker taking lead in Chicago, the musical?

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: A rock star takes the lead role in the Chicago musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocking chair is a rocker, so a chair can be one.

clue.text: Greyhound, maybe, in care of a church

parts.note: c/o, written CO, means care of

explanation.surface: A racing dog being looked after by a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhound is a long-distance bus company, so a Greyhound is an example of a coach.

clue.text: In which a monarch hid his approval to imprison one?

parts.note: his refers back to the monarch, so it means belonging to royalty

indicators.note: to imprison says one piece is shut inside the other

parts.note: OK signals approval
a means one

explanation.surface: A king hides away and gives the nod to locking someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles II hid in an oak tree after the Battle of Worcester, now called the Royal Oak.

clue.text: High spot, like going round Windy End

indicators.note: going round says the first piece surrounds the other

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: windy means twisting, so the letters wind into a new order

explanation.surface: A lofty place near the breezy end of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy End' reads like a place name, but 'Windy' is the anagram signal working on End.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are a South American mountain range, a lofty place in geography.

clue.text: Transported bird of prey — no alternative

indicators.note: no says this piece is missing from the bird

parts.note: a raptor is a bird of prey
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A hawk is shipped somewhere, with no other choice available.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means enraptured, carried away with delight, as transported does.

clue.text: Figure submitted an account over the phone

indicators.note: heard over the phone, words are judged by their sound alone

parts.note: to bill someone is to submit an account to them

explanation.surface: A figure sent in a bill by telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Build means physique, the shape of the body, as does figure.

clue.text: Player gets sack — supporter takes a pee

parts.note: a bag is a sack

indicators.note: takes says one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: a pier supports a bridge
P is a penny, spoken as pee

explanation.surface: A sportsman is fired while his trainer relieves himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagpiper plays the bagpipes, so is a musical player.

clue.text: Debut of Gordon Fish, the writer

indicators.note: the debut of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A writer reviews a fish dish served at a chef's opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Gide was a French author who won the Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Look into playing for money after sunset

indicators.note: into says the first word given goes inside the other

parts.note: gaming is gambling, playing for money
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Checking out the gambling tables once night has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is twilight, the dim time just after sunset.

clue.text: 'Seat of Government': article by ex-party leader

parts.note: the is the definite article
William Hague led the UK Conservative Party from 1997 to 2001

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a former leader titled 'Seat of Government'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hague is the Dutch city that houses the Netherlands' parliament and government.

clue.text: Gym equipment bays

definitions.meaning: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

explanation.definitionFit: Vaulting horses stand in a gymnasium, and bay is a common colour of horse.

clue.text: Boxer's punch that shows something's wrong

definitions.meaning: a boxing punch thrown across the body
a ... mark on homework indicates an error

explanation.surface: A fighter's blow that reveals something is amiss.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing a cross is a straight power punch; an X mark flags an incorrect answer.

clue.text: Rook — mouldy thing with loathsome wings

parts.note: a cast is something shaped in a mould

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A crow pictured as a rotten creature with hideous wings.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the rook is also called the castle.

clue.text: One of a poetic host's urns is cast almost sloppily

indicators.note: done sloppily means carelessly, so the letters are jumbled
almost means the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: Pots are cast carelessly by a potter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CAST to CAS; 'sloppily' scrambles URNS, IS and CAS. Wordsworth saw a host of golden daffodils.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcissus is the daffodil genus, the flower of Wordsworth's famous host.

clue.text: New start for fool, having no legal standing

indicators.note: a new start for a word swaps its first letter

parts.note: to gull is to fool or dupe

explanation.surface: A fresh beginning for a clown who has no legal status.
explanation.definitionFit: Null, as in null and void, means legally invalid and without force.

clue.text: Spirit needed by animal trainer

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lion tamer needs a stiff drink, or courage, to face the beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is short for malt whisky, a spirit.

clue.text: Sentimentality? Head off for boozer!

indicators.note: head off means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: slush is mawkish sentimentality

explanation.surface: A soppy drinker is told to leave for the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is slang for a heavy drinker.

clue.text: Censoring device forced rebel to suppress past record

indicators.note: to suppress here means to hold something down inside
forced means wrenched out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record, now a thing of the past

explanation.surface: A rebel is made to hide their old record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' gives BLEER, an arrangement the parse does not spell, which then holds the old record inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper sounds over swear words in broadcasts, censoring them.

clue.text: A cold calm way to disappear?

indicators.note: to disappear says these letters vanish from the larger word

parts.note: stillness is calm
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A cool, serene method of vanishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold is an example of a minor illness.
